Exuberant

ig-ZOO-ber-unt -- four syllables, stress on the second syllable, ZOO. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Exuberant is filled with lively energy.

The exuberant crowd of graduates tossed their caps so high the photographers lost them in the sun.

Worked Example

When the final buzzer sounds, the dance team does not just celebrate -- they cartwheel down the hallway, drum on the lockers, and sing the fight song at full volume until a janitor begs them to stop.

That overflowing, physical, cannot-hold-it-in energy is exuberant joy. Exuberant is not about what happened; it is about how much energy comes pouring out -- loud, lively, and impossible to miss.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

bubbly: Bubbly describes a personality's everyday sparkle -- someone cheerfully fizzy in ordinary conversation, week in and week out. Exuberant describes a single overflowing outburst: energy so full it spills out in motion and noise you can watch.

spirited: Spirited means showing liveliness and force -- a spirited debate or a spirited defense pushes back with energy. Exuberant is pure overflow: not fighting energy but celebrating energy, spilling out louder and larger than the moment requires.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

restrained: holding energy or feeling back

sluggish: slow-moving and low on energy

Where it sits · how far the energy overflows — lively → exuberant → rowdy

lively vs. exuberant: Lively is the mild, weaker word -- a lively conversation simply has energy in it -- while exuberant energy overflows: it bounces, shouts, and spills onto everything nearby.

rowdy vs. exuberant: Rowdy goes a step past exuberant: exuberant energy overflows in cheers and celebration, but rowdy energy turns disorderly -- pushing, crashing into things, leaving a mess behind.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ex-

prefix — ex-: out, thoroughly (Latin)

root — uber-

root — uber-: fertile, abundant (Latin uber)

suffix — -ant

suffix — -ant: being in a state of (Latin -antem)

Put it together

Put it together: Exuberant comes from Latin exuberare, 'to be abundantly fruitful' -- ex- ('thoroughly') plus uber ('fertile, overflowing'). An exuberant person's energy grows so abundantly that it spills over the edges, the way an overloaded orchard drops fruit.

Use the root in a new word: exuberance

Use the root in a new word: exuberance: Her exuberance filled the room before she said a single word.

Word Building

Word Choice

Exuberant is the cluster's most physical word: it describes joy you can watch -- bouncing, cheering, cartwheeling. Elated tells you how someone feels after good news; exuberant tells you what their energy is doing. A person can be quietly elated, but nobody is quietly exuberant.
